Title: Abandoned, Not Forgotten: Storytelling the Legacy of NASA's Discarded Equipment on the Moon and Mars
This project is an interactive 3D timeline that explores the human-made equipment and mission hardware left behind on the Moon and Mars after space exploration missions.
Visitors can move through a chronological timeline from Apollo 11 (1969) to Perseverance (2021), switch between Moon and Mars chapters, rotate and zoom simplified 3D models, and read short stories about each artifact's purpose and legacy — like lunar rovers, landers, scientific instruments, and landing-system components.
The main message of the project is: These objects are not just waste. Some were intentionally deployed for science, while others completed their mission task. Machines may stop working, but their discoveries live forever.
Technologies Used:HTML, CSS, JavaScript, http://Three.js
details:
🚀 ABANDONED, NOT FORGOTTEN
Let's go on a trip to the Moon and Mars!

Imagine this...

You are in space. Below you, Earth is shining. In front of you is the Moon — grey, quiet, and silent. And far away is Mars — red, dusty, and full of secrets.

Now, think about one question:
When astronauts came back home, where did their stuff go?

That is what my project is about!

🌕 First, Let's Visit the Moon
You click on the timeline, and you go back in time...
1969 — Apollo 11
Humans landed on the Moon for the first time! But do you know what happened? The lower part of the Eagle — the Descent Stage — is still there today. It finished its work and stayed there. Like it is saying, "I was here!"
1969 — Apollo 12 and Surveyor 3
This time, astronauts met an old robot — Surveyor 3. They picked up some of its parts and brought them back to Earth. Even a robot had a story to tell!
1969-1972 — Science Instruments
Astronauts placed instruments on the Moon to listen to moonquakes. This was not trash. This was science!
1971-1972 — Cars on the Moon!
Yes, cars drove on the Moon! They were called Lunar Roving Vehicles. Astronauts from Apollo 15, 16, and 17 drove them. When they left, the cars stayed there. They are still parked on the Moon today.

Can you imagine a car parked on the Moon? How cool is that?
🔴 Now, Let's Go to Mars!
The scene changes. Now everything is red. There is dust in the air. And the stories here are even more interesting.
1976 — Viking 1
The first spacecraft to work successfully on Mars. It took photos, checked the soil, and then it slept there forever.
1997 — Pathfinder and Sojourner
A very small robot called Sojourner. It was tiny, but very brave. It moved around and checked rocks and soil. It showed us that robots can drive on Mars!
2004 — Spirit and Opportunity
These were twin rovers. They searched for water on Mars. And they found it! They found signs that liquid water was there in the past. They worked for years, and then one day, they stopped. But their discovery is still alive.
2021 — Perseverance
When Perseverance landed, its heat shield, parachute, and backshell fell down. Their job was done. They stayed there — like they were saying, "We finished our mission."

🎮 What Can You Do in This Website?
This is not a boring website where you only read. You can _play_ with it!
- Click on the timeline — and travel in time
- Jump from Moon to Mars — change the planet in one click
- Rotate 3D models — drag them, zoom in, look closely
- Read the story — every object has its own small story
- Play the quiz — at the end, check how much you remember
And if the 3D does not load, don't worry — the full story is also written in text.

🛠️ How Did I Build It?
Let's look behind the scenes:
1. First, Research: I collected mission history from NASA websites
2. Then, Story Writing: I wrote a short story for each artifact
3. Then, Design:i decided how it should look — dark space, blue timeline, grey Moon, red Mars
4. Then, Website: I made the structure with HTML, and the beautiful look with CSS
5. Then, 3D: I used http://Three.js to make planets and models
6. Then, Connection: I connected timeline clicks to stories
7. Then, Quiz: I added a quiz to make learning fun
8. Finally, Testing: I checked everything — Is it working? Is it easy to read?
Technologies Used:HTML, CSS, JavaScript, http://Three.js

💡 What Do We Learn From This?
This project teaches us that:
- Going to space is very difficult
- Robots help us a lot
- Some things are not trash, they are history
- And technology can keep history alive
❤️ The Last Message
The things left on the Moon and Mars are not alone.
They say:
"Machines may stop working, but their discoveries live forever."
